title: Partition String by Equal Distinct Counts
statement:
You are given a string `s` made of lowercase English letters.

A **partition** of `s` cuts it into one or more non-empty contiguous parts whose concatenation is `s`. A partition is **balanced** if every part contains the same number of **distinct characters**. The shared number is not given in advance: it may be any value, as long as all parts agree on it.

Count the balanced partitions of `s`. Two partitions are different if they cut the string at different positions, and the partition that keeps the whole string as a single part also counts (it is trivially balanced).

Since the answer can be large, print it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the number of balanced partitions modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The balanced partitions are `aab` (one part with 2 distinct letters), `aa|b` (1 and 1) and `a|a|b` (1, 1 and 1). `a|ab` is not balanced because its parts have 1 and 2 distinct letters.
Balanced: `abab` (2 distinct), `ab|ab` (2 and 2) and `a|b|a|b` (1 each). Every other cut gives parts with different counts, for example `a|bab` has 1 and 2.

complexity.time: O(σ · n), where σ = 26 is the alphabet size

hints: Fix the common distinct count d and count only the partitions in which every part has exactly d distinct characters. Different d give different partitions, so the answers add up.

For a fixed d, let dp[i] be the number of ways to partition the prefix of length i. For a fixed end i, the start positions j where s[j..i) has exactly d distinct letters form one contiguous range, because the distinct count only grows as j moves left.

The range is bounded by the d-th and (d+1)-th most recent distinct letters before i (by last occurrence). Keep the last occurrences in a move-to-front list of at most 26 entries and use prefix sums of dp to sum over the range in O(1).
